text:
Justin Sourdif was one of last season's quiet success stories in Washington: 35 points and, by Evolving-Hockey's count, 2.2 wins above replacement, 42nd among 401 forwards with 500 or more minutes. The first month of this season has been slower. He has 4 points in 16 games, 3 goals and a single assist, and his scoring rate per 60 minutes is well below last year's.

There's more luck in that than slump. With him on the ice at five on five, the Capitals have taken 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) but scored 3.15 fewer goals than those chances deserved, which is where his missing assists went. His own shooting is running hot, 18.8%, so the goals may not keep pace. The rest of his game travels: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 70% of his exits leaving the zone with possession last season, and 19% of his setups came from behind the net, against 8% for a typical forward. Evolving-Hockey also credited him with taking chances away and drawing more penalties than he takes.
